 IMD Cyclone Arnab Alert: Bay of Bengal Storm Becomes India's 1st Cyclone of 2026, Red Alert in These Areas; When, Where is Landfall
 By Jaisal Kaur Last Updated: Oct 26, 2026, 14:12 IST A developing weather system over the Bay of Bengal has intensified into a cyclonic storm by October 26, thus causing the India Meteorological Department (IMD) to declare a rainfall alert for coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha. If the system turns into a cyclone as predicted, it will be named Arnab, according to the regional cyclone naming scheme.
 The IMD stated that a low-pressure area formed over the east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal on October 23 
 As Cyclone Arnab had formed today morning over Bay of Bengal, IMD Visakhapatnam director PLN Murty said, “It has intensified from a deep depression into a cyclonic storm, is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam by the forenoon of October 28, bringing strong winds and heavy rainfall to coastal Andhra Pradesh.” 
 IMD has issued a red-level cyclone warning for Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha for today.

 — Press Trust of India (@PTI_News) October 26, 2026 Satellite images features the cyclone’s tightly wound cloud bands and a separate central circulation over the Bay of Bengal, highlighting the organised storm system as it bolsters. 
 Earlier, the IMD had cautioned that a developing weather system over the Bay of Bengal could develop into Cyclone Arnab by October 26, 2026, thus triggering heavy rainfall in coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha. The system is likely to turn towards the north Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts over the next two days.  
 Cyclone Arnab Alert: IMD Forecasts Heavy Rain in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha 
 A developing weather system over the Bay of Bengal is slated to intensify into a cyclonic storm by October 26, thus causing the India Meteorological Department (IMD) to declare a rainfall alert for coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha. If the system turns into a cyclone as predicted, it will be named Arnab, according to the regional cyclone naming scheme. 
 Bay of Bengal System to Develop into a Cyclone  
 The IMD stated that a low-pressure area formed over the east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal on October 23. The system is likely to aggravate into a depression on October 24, succeeded by a deep depression on October 25. 
 By the morning of October 26, it could develop into a cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal. The system is then predicted to shift west-northwestwards towards north Andhra Pradesh and nearby south Odisha coasts over the comming two days. 
 Heavy Rain Alert for States 
 According to the IMD's prediction, coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha could see heavy to extremely heavy rainfall between October 27 and 29. The developing system may also cause thunderstorms, lightning, and powerful winds in adjacent coastal areas. 
 The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority has cautioned about rainfall across numerous districts, including Vizianagaram, Manyam, Alluri, Kadapa, Annamayya, Chittoor and Tirupati.  
 Odisha is also slated to see enhanced rainfall activity as the system nears the coast. Heavy showers could trigger waterlogging, localised flooding and disturbance to transport in low-lying areas. 
 Current IMD Alerts & Forecasts for Heavy Rainfall 
 • Orange Warning (Heavy to Very Heavy Rain): Kerala, Mahe, Lakshadweep, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and Karaikal. 
 • Heavy Rainfall: Andaman and Nicobar Islands and South Interior Karnataka. 
 • Thunderstorms, Lightning & Gusty Winds: Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh, Punjab, Rajasthan, Konkan, Goa, Andhra Pradesh, and Lakshadweep, as well as Coastal Karnataka. 
 • Bay of Bengal System / Cyclonic Alert: A low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal moving toward the North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha coasts by October 28, could alsot bring showers in West Bengal, Jharkhand, Bihar, and Chhattisgarh. 
 Landfall Details for Cyclone Arnab 
 Cyclone Arnab is expected to make landfall on October 28, 2026. 
 • Date: October 28, 2026 (afternoon/night) 
 • Expected Location: Along the coast between northern Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha 
 How Cyclone Arnab Got Its Name 
 The name Arnab was proposed by Bangladesh and is listed in the formal list of tropical cyclone names adopted in April 2020 by the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) and the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) Panel on Tropical Cyclones. 
 The list contains names given by 13 countries: Bangladesh, India, Iran, the Maldives, Myanmar, Oman, Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Sri Lanka, Thailand, the United Arab Emirates and Yemen. 
 The name Arnab is generally linked with the Bengali word for the ocean or sea. However, the formal IMD naming list confirms the country that proposed the name and its pronunciation but does not offer a definition of the word.
